paper: Causal Modeling of Selection in Evolution

claims.paper_claim: Definition 1: the evolutionary selection model has four edge types
claims.evidence: One T=2 graph contains trait, reproduction, heritable-factor, and inheritance edges.
claims.limitation: One hand-built graph does not validate general definitions, semantics, or assumptions.

claims.paper_claim: Lemma 1: evolutionary selection can induce dependencies absent from the static graph
claims.evidence: G+ is a supergraph in three hand-built cases, with strict extra edges in two.
claims.limitation: No generated evolutionary data or general lemma proof is provided.

claims.paper_claim: Theorem 1: G+ represents selected evolutionary d-separations
claims.evidence: 36 singleton/empty-set comparisons across three T=2 graphs have zero mismatches.
claims.limitation: Arbitrary sets, generations, conditioning sets, and assumptions are not checked.

claims.paper_claim: Theorem 2: PC/GES interpretations are sound under paper assumptions
claims.evidence: The local oracle skeleton has zero wrongly removed true edges in three cases.
claims.limitation: No observational data, PC/GES implementation, faithfulness check, or precision experiment is present.

claims.paper_claim: Theorem 4: multi-domain identification is sound and complete
claims.evidence: The same local relation is returned under two labels using the same graph.
claims.limitation: There is no domain shift, data, or CDNOD procedure; this is an internal consistency check.

claims.paper_claim: Section 5.2: seven real-world datasets support the interpretation
claims.evidence: No corresponding dataset run exists in this checkout.
claims.limitation: DGRP, Cranial, Panzea, PanTHERIA, AVONET, CSES, and PUMS analyses are absent.
